title: JEPA-v2 pretraining of the spectrum encoder (J4)
axis: initialisation of the spectrum encoder: random (A0), JEPA-v2 with context and m/z queries (A1), JEPA ctx-free control (A2); everything else identical (work/w4, --val work/cells, wm-canon recipe, 31k steps, seed 0)
question: Does masked-peak latent prediction pretraining make the fine-tuned model rank natural products better against full PubChem windows, and does the gain need the spectrum context?
hypothesis: A1 beats A0 on np_c2 (primary) without losing on np_tims, and A1 beats A2.

rules.leak_policy: every arm leak-free (spectra, init encoder, anchors) on every cell, else void
rules.consequence: jepa_helps -> the JEPA-v2 checkpoint becomes the bundle candidate for the LB probe; otherwise the bundle keeps A0
limitations: one seed per arm (seed differences so far: holdout 0.002, np_tims fused 0.001)
pretraining budget 20k steps x 512 spectra (~2.3 h on the 3060)
